name: Gurugram Tech Employee Unpaid Salary & Relieving Letter Withheld
raw_input: I worked as a frontend developer at an IT consultancy firm in Cyber City, Gurugram for 18 months at Rs 70,000/month. I submitted my resignation on 1st August 2024 and completed my full 60-day notice period till 30th September 2024. All project handovers and company assets (MacBook, ID card) were handed over and I received an asset clearance certificate from IT. My August salary was delayed, and my September salary plus 15 days encashable leave (total Rs 1,65,000) has not been paid. It has been 50 days since my last working day. Whenever I email HR, they say 'finance team is facing client payment delays'. More importantly, they are withholding my Relieving Letter and Experience Certificate. My new employer is threatening to cancel my job offer if I don't submit my relieving letter by end of this week. I have my appointment letter, resignation acceptance email, and signed clearance form.

case_dossier.case_title: Unpaid Salary and Withholding Relieving Letter after Resignation
case_dossier.summary: The former frontend developer completed a 60‑day notice period and returned all company assets, but the employer has not paid the September salary and leave encashment totaling Rs 1,65,000 and is refusing to issue the relieving and experience letters, jeopardising the new job offer.

rights_advice.plain_language_standing:
You have a clear legal right to receive the salary and leave encashment that you earned up to your last working day. Under the Code on Wages, 2019, an employer must pay all wages due within two working days of the employee’s removal, dismissal, retrenchment or resignation (Section 17(2)). The amount you are owed – August and September salary plus 15 days of leave encashment – is therefore a civil debt that the employer is legally bound to pay. The same Code also says that no deduction can be made from your wages unless it is expressly authorised (Section 18(1)), so the employer cannot withhold any part of your salary as an excuse for client payment delays.

In addition, refusing to give you a relieving or experience letter after you have completed your notice period and returned all company property is not a criminal matter; it is a breach of the employment contract and can be pursued as a civil claim for specific performance or damages. The law treats these issues as civil disputes, not cheating under the criminal code, so the appropriate remedy is through labour‑related civil forums rather than a police complaint.

governing_laws.relevance: Requires employer to pay all wages (including salary and leave encashment) within two working days of resignation
Preserves any other time‑limits for wage payment that may be prescribed by state rules
Prohibits unauthorised deductions from wages, preventing the employer from withholding salary as a penalty

governing_laws.act_name: General Legal Principle (Civil vs. Criminal Boundary)
governing_laws.relevance: Clarifies that non‑payment of salary or refusal to issue relieving letters is a civil dispute, not a criminal cheating case

action_options.title: Send Formal Legal Notice (Email / Registered Post)
action_options.cost_estimate: Free to minimal (postage or email cost)
action_options.details: Draft a concise notice stating: (a) amount owed (Rs 1,65,000), (b) demand payment within 7 days, (c) demand issuance of relieving and experience letters within the same period, (d) mention that under Section 17(2) of the Code on Wages you are entitled to immediate payment, and (e) warn that failure will lead to filing a claim before the Labour Commissioner and DLSA. Attach copies of appointment letter, resignation acceptance, asset clearance certificate, and any HR correspondence. Send via registered post and email, and keep proof of delivery.

action_options.title: File a Grievance on the Labour Ministry’s e‑Daakhil / Labour Commissioner Portal
action_options.cost_estimate: Zero court fees for claims up to Rs 5 Lakhs
action_options.details: Register on the Ministry of Labour’s e‑Daakhil portal (or the state labour department portal). Upload the legal notice, supporting documents, and a brief statement of facts. Select ‘Recovery of Wages and Issuance of Relieving Letter’ as the grievance type. The Labour Commissioner will issue a notice to the employer to comply within a stipulated period (usually 15 days).

action_options.title: Approach the District Labour Court / DLSA for Recovery of Wages and Specific Performance
action_options.timeline: Within 60‑90 days if earlier steps fail
action_options.cost_estimate: Nominal court fees (around Rs 500‑1,000) plus any filing charges; you may get free legal aid from DLSA
action_options.details: Prepare a plaint citing Section 17(2) and Section 18(1) of the Code on Wages, attach all evidence (notice, emails, asset clearance, salary slips, bank statements). File the suit in the appropriate District Labour Court or approach the District Legal Services Authority for free legal aid. The court can order payment of the pending salary, interest, and direct the employer to issue the relieving and experience letters. You may represent yourself, but a lawyer can help with drafting and representation, especially if the employer contests the claim.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: You can start by sending the legal notice and filing the e‑Daakhil grievance yourself; these steps do not require a lawyer. However, if the employer does not comply and you need to file a suit in the Labour Court or seek enforcement of the court’s order, engaging a qualified labour‑law advocate is advisable. A lawyer will ensure the plaint is correctly drafted, help you navigate procedural rules, and represent you effectively in court.
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self‑advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

legal_notice_draft:
**[Your Name]**  
Frontend Developer (Former Employee)  
Flat No. ___, [Building Name], [Street],  
[Locality], [City] – [Pin Code]  
Mobile: [Your Mobile No.] | Email: [Your Email]  

---

### LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE  

**Date:** ____ ____ 2026  

**Mode of Dispatch:** Speed Post (Speed Post with Acknowledgement Due) / Registered Email (with read‑receipt)  

**To,**  

**The Managing Director / HR Head**  
[Employer’s Company Name] – IT Consultancy Firm  
[Company’s Registered Office Address]  
[City] – [Pin Code]  

---

#### 1. UNDER INSTRUCTIONS FROM MY CLIENT  

The undersigned, **[Your Full Name]**, hereby issues this legal notice on behalf of himself/herself (the “Complainant”) pursuant to the provisions of the **Code on Wages, 2019** and the principles of natural justice, demanding immediate settlement of the dues and issuance of the relieving & experience letters as detailed below.

---

#### 2. FACTUAL MATRIX  

| No. | Date / Period | Event |
|-----|---------------|-------|
| 1 | **Feb 2023 – July 2024** | Employed as Front‑End Developer on a salary of **Rs 70,000 per month**. |
| 2 | **1 Aug 2024** | Submitted resignation via email (copy annexed). |
| 3 | **1 Aug – 30 Sep 2024** | Served the contractual **60‑day notice period**, completed all hand‑overs and returned company assets (MacBook, ID card). |
| 4 | **30 Sep 2024** | Received **Asset Clearance Certificate** from IT department (annexed). |
| 5 | **Early Sep 2024** | August salary was delayed; later paid on ___ (if paid). |
| 6 | **By 19 Nov 2024** (≈ 85 days after last working day) | September salary **plus 15 days encashable leave** (total **Rs 1,65,000**) remains unpaid. |
| 7 | **Since Sep 2024** | HR repeatedly states that the finance team is awaiting client payments; no salary credited. |
| 8 | **Early Nov 2024** | Employer refuses to issue **Relieving Letter** and **Experience Certificate**; new employer has demanded the relieving letter by the end of the week. |

---

#### 3. EVIDENCE IN POSSESSION  

The following documents are annexed hereto and form part of the present notice:  

- **Annexure‑A:** Appointment Letter.  
- **Annexure‑B:** Resignation Acceptance Email (dated 1 Aug 2024).  
- **Annexure‑C:** Signed Asset Clearance Certificate (dated 30 Sep 2024).  
- **Annexure‑D:** Email correspondence with HR regarding salary delay (Sept – Nov 2024).  
- **Annexure‑E:** Copy of the resignation email sent on 1 Aug 2024.  

*The complainant also possesses the following documents which can be produced on demand:* salary slips for Aug‑Sep 2024, bank/UPI statements showing non‑receipt of September salary, company policy on notice‑period salary & leave encashment, any written refusal of relieving/experience letters, and the offer letter of the new employer indicating the deadline.

---

#### 4. LEGAL BASIS OF THE CLAIM  

1. **Section 17(2), Code on Wages, 2019** – mandates that an employer shall pay **all wages** (including salary and leave encashment) **within two working days** of the employee’s resignation.  

2. **Section 18(1), Code on Wages, 2019** – prohibits any unauthorised deduction from wages; therefore the employer cannot withhold salary on the pretext of client payment delays.  

3. The refusal to issue the relieving and experience letters, after the employee has fully complied with the notice period and returned all assets, constitutes a **breach of the employment contract** and entitles the employee to specific performance and damages under the Indian Contract Act, 1872.  

4. The claim is a **civil debt** recoverable before the Labour Commissioner/Labour Court; it is **not a criminal matter** under the Indian Penal Code.

---

#### 5. DEMAND  

In view of the foregoing facts and law, the Complainant **HEREBY DEMANDS**:

1. **Payment of the pending dues** – **Rs 1,65,000** (September salary + 15 days leave encashment) **within fifteen (15) days** from the receipt of this notice.  

2. **Issuance of the Relieving Letter and Experience Certificate** in the prescribed format **within the same fifteen (15)‑day period**.  

3. **Statutory interest** at **12 % per annum** (simple interest) on the amount due from **30 Sep 2024** till actual payment, together with **costs of litigation** (court fees, postage, attorney’s fees) if the matter proceeds to court.

---

#### 6. CONSEQUENCES OF NON‑COMPLIANCE  

Should the Employer fail to comply with the above demands **within 15 days**, the Complainant will be constrained to initiate the following actions **without any further notice**:

| Sr. No. | Action | Forum | Anticipated Consequence |
|--------|--------|-------|------------------------|
| 1 | File a grievance on the **Labour Ministry’s e‑Daakhil / State Labour Commissioner portal** for recovery of wages and specific performance. | Labour Commissioner | Issuance of a statutory notice to the employer; possible attachment of assets. |
| 2 | Institute a suit before the **District Labour Court / DLSA** for recovery of wages, interest, damages, and specific performance (issuance of relieving/experience letters). | District Labour Court | Court decree for payment of dues with 12 % interest, costs, and an order directing issuance of the letters. |
| 3 | Seek **legal aid** from the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) under **NALSA** (Helpline 15100) if the Complainant is unable to bear litigation costs. | DLSA | Free legal representation and assistance. |

The above steps will be taken **without prejudice** to any other remedy available under law, including filing a complaint under the **Industrial Disputes Act, 1947** or approaching the **National Consumer Helpline** for violation of consumer rights.

---

#### 7. DECLARATION  

The Complainant declares that the contents of this notice are true and correct to the best of his/her knowledge and belief, and that he/she is ready to pursue all legal remedies available under the law.

---

#### 8. SIGNATURE  

```

[Your Full Name]  
Former Front‑End Developer  
Date: ____/____/2026
```

---

sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Under employment laws, full and final dues must be cleared timely and withholding my relieving letter violates my right to livelihood. If my Rs 1,65,000 and relieving letter are not issued within 3 days, I will file a formal complaint with the District Labor Commissioner.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Sir, we understand your concern, but as per our internal policy the final settlement is processed only after the finance team completes its clearance, which normally takes up to 10 working days. We have already made certain deductions for the notice period and asset usage as per the signed agreement. However, if you forward us the signed resignation copy and the asset‑return receipt, we will expedite the process and aim to release the pending Rs 1,65,000 and your relieving/experience letters by 7 December. Please note that any legal notice will be reviewed by our legal department before any further action.
